text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The case against alleged war criminal Aleksandras Lileikis might be halted after a medical commission concluded that further legal procedures might be dangerous to his health.
- Sixtry-three of the 98 illegal imigrants who escaped Pabrade camp were detained on Monday. It is thought that another 35 have escaped from the country.
- Litimpeks Bank had 4.23 million litas in losses in the first half of 1997.
- Vilniaus Bank posted a 21.4 million litas net profit for the first half of the year.
- The head of the EU PHARE programme's state administration and municipal reform department was robbed when two armed criminals broke into his hotel room. Two suspects are in custody.
- The agricultural ministry said that Lithuania has more than enough sugar until the next harvest and may auction excess supplies. The country consumes around 100,000 tonnes of sugar per year.
- Mazheikiu Nafta refined 1.551 million tonnes of crude in the first half of 1997.
